To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a multiple barrier layer tablet dosage form can be successfully developed for controlled delivery of highly water-solubles drug like ropinirole HCl.

a novel multiple barrier layer tablet dosage form was successfully developed for controlled release of ropinirole hydrocholride and the formulation was found to be effective in vivo and the in vitro–in vitro correlation was established.
the multiple barrier layer tablet dosage form can effectively control in vitro burst release of highly water-solable drugs and can also be used to develop generic formulations of the drug.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the controlled release of a highly water-solubility drug ropinirole hydrocloride from a multiple barrier layer tablet dosage form.
developing a multiple barrier layer tablet dosage form for ropinirole hydrocholoride with controlled release profile to avoid dose dumping and establishing in vitro-in vivo correlation.
the development of a controlled release dosage form for ropinirole hydrocloride using hypromellose as a polymer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a multiple barrier layer tablet dosage form is a viable and effective approach to control the burst effect of the water-soluble drugs.

a multiple barrier layer tablet dosage form can be used for controlled release of ropinirole hydrocholoride and a level A correlation between in vitro dissolution data and in vivo data can be achieved.
the technology is suitable for the controlled release of highly water-solubility drug ropinirole HCl and can be scaled up for manufacturing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the technology can be used to develop multiple barrier layer tablets with controlled release of ropinirole hydrocholoride.
a multiple barrier layer tablet dosage form can be used to control the in vitro burst effect and can be used for the development of immediate release and controlled release formulations.
in vitro–in vitro correlation is a good tool for formulation optimization and can be used as surrogate to in vivo correlation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the in vivo pharmacokinetic studies are essential for the establishment of IVIVC even when the dissolution profiles of different formulations are similar.
in vitro–in vitro correlation is possible for different formulation technology with same drug.
the technology can be applied for any drug that exhibits burst effect in vitro.
